inline_comments.comment: `inferAgent(values.model)` is invoked at module top-level before Zod validation runs (line 76). If `values.model` is an unrecognised string, `inferAgent` throws a raw `Error` that bypasses the user-friendly `parsed.error.issues` reporting block entirely and crashes with an unhelpful stack trace. Wrap the inference in a try/catch and surface it through the same error path, or move the agent resolution inside the `safeParse` call so Zod handles the unknown-model case.

`PROJECTS.find((p) => p.name === args.project)!` uses a non-null assertion to silence the `undefined` case. Although Zod validates `args.project` against `PROJECT_NAMES`, the assertion still suppresses TypeScript's safety net. Per project rules, test-infrastructure scripts must not use `!` to paper over absence — add an explicit guard: `if (!project) { logger.log(...); process.exit(1); }`. This also avoids a potential runtime error if `PROJECTS` and `PROJECT_NAMES` ever fall out of sync.

Both `getComponentCandidates` and `runGhostStories` are imported via deep relative paths (`../../../code/core/src/core-server/utils/ghost-stories/...`). The same PR exports these symbols from `storybook/internal/core-server` (see `code/core/src/core-server/index.ts`), and `grading-helpers.test.ts` correctly uses that public export. Per project rules, cross-package imports must go through the public package export — change to `import { getComponentCandidates, runGhostStories } from 'storybook/internal/core-server'`. Deep paths are fragile under restructuring and bypass the intended API surface.

All five `vi.mock(...)` calls use the factory-replacement form (`() => ({ fn: vi.fn() })`). Project rules require `vi.mock('module', { spy: true })` at the top level, with mock behaviour configured via `.mockImplementation(...)` / `.mockResolvedValue(...)` exclusively inside `beforeEach` — never inside individual test bodies. In particular, the 'does not call grade before agent finishes' test (around line 147) sets up `mockImplementation` inline, which bleeds between tests. Refactor to the spy pattern with a top-level `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach`.

`const effort = variant.effort as 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max';` is a redundant type assertion — `variant.effort` is already narrowed to `ClaudeEffort` (which is exactly that union) by the `if (variant.agent !== 'claude')` guard above. Remove the cast; if the SDK's `effort` parameter has a different type, prefer `@ts-expect-error` with a comment explaining the upstream gap over a silent `as`.

`debug: true` is hardcoded in the Claude execution config. This forces verbose SDK output for every benchmark run, regardless of whether the user passed `--verbose`. The `ClaudeExecutionConfig` interface defines `debug: boolean`, so it is already designed to be configurable. Either drive this from the `TrialConfig.verbose` flag or default it to `false` and only set it to `true` when `verbose` is enabled.

`promptName || 'setup'` (also at line 80) uses logical-OR instead of nullish coalescing. `promptName` is typed as `string`, so an explicitly passed empty string `''` would fall back to `'setup'` silently. Use `promptName ?? 'setup'` (or simply `promptName` if the type guarantees it is non-empty after CLI validation). The project rule is to prefer `??` over `||` for default fallbacks.

`EVAL_ROOT` is hardcoded to `../storybook-eval` relative to the monorepo root. There is no environment-variable override, so anyone with a different directory layout (CI, different clone location, Windows path) must edit source to change it. Add `process.env.STORYBOOK_EVAL_ROOT ?? resolve(REPO_ROOT, '..', 'storybook-eval')` so the path is configurable without code changes.

`getRemoteBranchHead` performs a `git ls-remote` network call on **every** run that could reuse the cache (i.e., whenever `.git` and the cache metadata exist). This adds latency even when nothing has changed. Consider making the freshness check opt-in via a `--check-updates` flag, or caching the remote HEAD locally with a short TTL (e.g., a timestamp in the cache metadata), so back-to-back runs are not blocked on a network round-trip.

`parseGitDiffStatus` silently falls back to `'M'` for any unrecognised git status code. If git emits an unexpected line format (e.g., merge conflicts, submodule markers), the entry is silently classified as 'modified' with no warning. Consider logging a diagnostic or returning a distinct sentinel so callers can decide how to handle unknown statuses rather than silently continuing with incorrect data.

All six benchmark repos point to personal forks under `kasperpeulen/` rather than an official `storybookjs/` organisation. If these forks diverge, are deleted, or become private, the eval harness silently breaks for all contributors. The PR description says these are 'forked repos' — they should be transferred to a canonical org (e.g., `storybookjs-eval/`) or at minimum documented as the authoritative eval source with an explicit maintenance plan.

Changing `resource_class` from `small` to `large` significantly increases CI compute cost (and queue time). This change is unrelated to the eval harness and there is no explanation in the PR description or a comment here. Add an inline comment explaining why `large` is now required, or move this to a separate PR with justification.

general_comments.comment: `citty` is added to `scripts/package.json` (and locked in `yarn.lock`) but is never imported anywhere in the eval harness code. The CLI argument parsing uses `node:util`'s `parseArgs` instead. Remove the unused dependency to avoid confusion and unnecessary install weight.

The PR description prominently describes `eval-parallel.ts` ('all 8 combos: node scripts/eval/eval-parallel.ts -p mealdrop') and the live-prefixed log output it produces, but the file is absent from the diff. Similarly, the Google Sheets upload feature (`EVAL_GOOGLE_SHEETS_URL`) is described but has no implementation in the diff. The `scripts/tsconfig.json` excludes `eval/google-apps-script.js`, hinting at further planned code. If these are deferred to follow-up PRs, the PR description should say so explicitly; if they were accidentally omitted, they should be included before merge so the harness is actually runnable end-to-end as described.

The `grade.test.ts` file declares `vi.mock(...)` for `getComponentCandidates` and `runGhostStories` at the top, but none of the test cases in that file configure, call, or assert on those mocks — the file only tests pure utility functions (`filterStorybookFiles`, `computeQualityScore`, `countTypeCheckErrors`, `parseChangedFiles`). The mocks exist solely to prevent transitive import failures when `grade.ts` is loaded. Per project rules, verify that the real implementations cannot simply be allowed to load (they are function definitions with no module-level side effects). If the mocks are still needed, add a comment explaining why, so future readers do not mistake them for tested behaviour.
